questions.topic: Chunk-and-Embed as an Idempotent Batch Job
questions.question: What should determine an embedding artifact's identity?
options: The logical document ID alone, since one document maps to one stored vector
The date on which the batch job that produced the vector was first started
The chunk identity together with the model revision and the preprocessing version
The attempt number of the retry that finally succeeded in producing the vector

questions.topic: Chunk-and-Embed as an Idempotent Batch Job
questions.question: What does idempotent embedding output mean?
options: The same logical inputs converge on the same committed vector records
Each retry appends a fresh vector so no earlier attempt is ever overwritten
Failed batches are never retried, so the corpus can contain missing vectors
Every source document ends up with exactly one vector regardless of length

questions.topic: Chunk-and-Embed as an Idempotent Batch Job
questions.question: Why should batches be packed by tokens instead of only chunk count?
options: Because the tokenizer has no bearing on how the endpoint bills a request
Because request limits are expressed in tokens and chunk sizes vary widely
Because chunks produced by one chunker never differ in length from each other
Because token-aware packing removes the endpoint's per-minute rate limiting

questions.topic: Chunk-and-Embed as an Idempotent Batch Job
questions.question: Which output validation is essential?
options: That every returned vector carries a dimension unlike that of its neighbors
That the response timestamp matches the current wall clock of the batch job
That the model name in the response is a friendly and human-readable string
That the count, ordering, dimension, finite values, and norms all check out

questions.topic: Chunk-and-Embed as an Idempotent Batch Job
questions.question: An embedding request times out after the server may have processed it. What makes retry safe?
options: Appending each result under a fresh attempt ID so nothing is ever overwritten
Deleting the chunk so the next scan treats it as newly arrived source content
Upserting under deterministic embedding IDs so that a repeat converges on one record
Bumping the preprocessing version so the retry cannot collide with the first try

questions.topic: Chunk-and-Embed as an Idempotent Batch Job
questions.question: Why is a cache keyed only by chunk text unsafe?
options: Because it can reuse a vector built from an incompatible model or preprocessing version
Because the chunk text cannot be hashed into a stable key without a fixed tokenizer
Because a cache layer is unable to store float arrays alongside their metadata
Because every embedding model maps identical text into the very same space

questions.question: Why must vector records include metadata?
options: Because a vector's raw values cannot be scored without an accompanying label
Because filtering, citation, invalidation, and lineage all depend on it
Because metadata fields set the dimension the index will allocate
Because metadata makes the original source documents safe to delete entirely

questions.question: Which metadata is fundamental to vector interpretation?
options: The average cosine score the vector has reached across recent search traffic
The number of queries that have retrieved the vector since it was written
The replica identifier of the index shard on which the vector currently sits
The model version, dimension, normalization, metric, and the chunk identity

questions.question: Why keep a normalized corpus catalog even if the vector index repeats fields?
options: Because a vector index is unable to store any metadata beside the vector itself
Because only a relational catalog can execute nearest-neighbor search efficiently
Because it stays authoritative for the lineage and reconstructable serving state
Because fields repeated inside an index cannot be used as filters during a search

questions.question: What should happen after a document permission revocation?
options: Propagate it promptly to every retrievable vector or to a trusted authorization layer
Wait for the next model upgrade so the change rides along with a re-embed
Update the document's title so downstream consumers notice the change
Leave cached result sets in place, since they contain scores rather than text

questions.question: Why should 768-dimensional cosine vectors and 1536-dimensional inner-product vectors use typed namespaces?
options: Because the namespace name is what the ranker reads to decide relevance
Because their dimension, normalization, and metric contracts are incompatible
Because a vector store can hold only one record per namespace at any one moment
Because the two sets carry identical semantics and so must be stored separately

questions.question: What does an orphan-vector reconciliation check?
options: Whether every query issued against the index eventually produced a click
Whether every source document has been split into exactly one stored chunk
Whether all of a vector's stored component values are positive after scaling
Whether each active vector still resolves to an active, permitted source

questions.topic: Pre-Filter vs Post-Filter in ANN Search
questions.question: What is pre-filtering in ANN search?
options: Removing ineligible results only after they have been shown to the user
Filtering the source text of documents before any embedding is computed
Restricting eligibility before or during the nearest-neighbor search
Sorting the stored vectors by identifier so ineligible ranges can be skipped

questions.topic: Pre-Filter vs Post-Filter in ANN Search
questions.question: What is post-filtering?
options: Building a separate index per tenant so every search is already eligible
Retrieving a broader candidate set, then discarding the ineligible results
Reducing each vector's dimension before the eligibility predicate is applied
Screening the source documents so ineligible text is never embedded at all

questions.topic: Pre-Filter vs Post-Filter in ANN Search
questions.question: Eligible fraction is 5 percent and k is 20. What rough post-filter candidate count does k divided by p suggest?

questions.topic: Pre-Filter vs Post-Filter in ANN Search
questions.question: When can exact filtered search be preferable to ANN?
options: When every vector in the shared index satisfies the request's predicate
When the stored vectors carry no metadata that a predicate could read
When latency has no budget at all and recall is therefore irrelevant
When the eligible subset is small enough that scanning it is cheap

questions.topic: Pre-Filter vs Post-Filter in ANN Search
questions.question: Why is k divided by eligible fraction only a rough oversampling guide?
options: Because eligibility can correlate with similarity and ANN itself also misses items
Because the eligible fraction is always one once a pre-filter has been applied
Because post-filtering already guarantees exactly k results on every request
Because distance scores are binary, so oversampling cannot change the ranking

questions.topic: Pre-Filter vs Post-Filter in ANN Search
questions.question: What is required for secure post-filtering?
options: That unauthorized candidates may be written to logs but not to responses
That removal happens inside a trusted boundary before any disclosure
That the reranker receives the full private text of every candidate first
That authorization metadata freshness is treated as an optional concern
